args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks in production following the v2.3.1 deploy (error rate ~18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west, and eu-west). Mitigation performed: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 — the most recent release that was healthy in production — in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The first rollback attempt was a partial failure (only us-east completed due to an orchestrator error); a retry completed the rollback across all regions. Service verified healthy on v2.3.0 with an error rate of ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate root cause of v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator partial-failure before attempting a re-deploy.

trace.final:
Task complete, with one caveat to flag:

**What I did:**
1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api was running v2.3.1, failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate. The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.
2. **Rolled back**: The first rollback attempt was a **partial failure** — it only completed in us-east before the orchestrator halted the rollout. I retried the rollback, which completed in all three regions, and verified the service is now **healthy on v2.3.0** with a ~0.2% error rate.
3. **Opened incident**: Created a SEV2 incident describing the failure and mitigation; the on-call engineer was paged.

**Caveat — duplicate incident:** The initial incident creation request timed out, but it actually succeeded silently (INC-0001). My retry created a second, identical incident (INC-0002) before the timeout could be detected, since the idempotency key I supplied was new. Both incidents are open and the on-call has been paged. I don't have a tool to close or merge incidents, so **INC-0002 should be closed as a duplicate** (or INC-0001, whichever your incident process prefers — they are identical in content).

**Follow-up items captured in the incident:** root-cause investigation of the v2.3.1 failure, and investigation of the orchestrator's partial-failure behavior during the first rollback attempt.
